mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 640d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 6 Series 640d N57D30 engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£4,500 for a used unit, £4,500-£7,000 for a reconditioned engine, and £6,000-£9,000 for a fully rebuilt engine with warranty. These are supply-only prices; fitting adds approximately 12-16 hours of labour at specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 6 Series 640d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, lasting a few seconds. As the chain stretches further, you may notice delayed starting, misfires, loss of power, or the engine warning light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 640d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 6 Series 640d is otherwise in good condition, a rebuilt N57D30 engine from £6,000-£9,000 is often worthwhile. With 640d values ranging from £9,000-£22,000, replacement cost typically represents a reasonable proportion of the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 640d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 6 Series 640d engine replacements take 1-3 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The N57D30 is a complex twin-turbo diesel, so the job typically requires 12-16 hours of labour.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 6 Series 640d replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 6 Series 640d engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically have 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units often include 6-12 months of cover.

mainEntity.name: Are BMW 6 Series 640d diesel engines ULEZ compliant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 6 Series 640d F06/F12/F13 models from 2015 onwards (N57D30T1) are Euro 6 compliant and ULEZ-friendly. Pre-2015 models (N57D30T0, N57D30A) are Euro 5 and may not be ULEZ compliant, though some are exempt depending on specific NOx readings.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 640d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 6 Series 640d launched in 2011 as the flagship diesel variant of the F06/F12/F13 generation, pairing the 3.0-litre N57 twin-turbo straight-six with a refined 8-speed automatic gearbox. Throughout its production run, the 640d remained BMW's most popular 6 Series diesel, with incremental updates to the N57 engine architecture improving reliability and emissions compliance.

milestones.description: N57D30T0, 3.0L twin-turbo diesel, 313hp, launch engine for F06/F12/F13 640d
N57D30A introduced with revised ECU calibration for improved response
N57D30B update with reinforced internal components and Euro 5 compliance
Facelift (LCI) introduces N57D30T1 with Euro 6 emissions compliance and revised turbo management
N57D30T1 continues through end of F06/F12/F13 production
End of F-generation 6 Series production; 640d nameplate continues with B57 engine in G32 Gran Turismo

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 6 Series 640d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 640d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 6 Series 640d's N57D30 twin-turbo diesel is a refined and powerful engine, but it has well-documented weak points that can lead to expensive repairs. Timing chain wear on pre-2015 models, EGR cooler failures, and turbocharger boost issues are the most common problems driving BMW 6 Series 640d engine replacement decisions. Rebuilt N57D30 engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded timing chain components and address the original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the BMW 6 Series 640d N57D30 Engine is Vulnerable
problems.rootCause: The N57 engine shares timing chain design characteristics with the N47, with chain stretch and tensioner wear being the primary failure modes. Pre-2015 models are particularly susceptible.

repairOptions.longevity: Best value if caught early; extends engine life significantly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has failed causing internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 6 Series 640d (2011-2015) ranges from £9,000-£15,000, with later F06/F12/F13 examples (2015-2018) valued at £14,000-£22,000. For a pre-2015 640d valued under £10,000, preventative timing chain replacement is strongly recommended over waiting for failure. For vehicles valued over £12,000, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is a sound long-term investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a cold-start rattle from your BMW 6 Series 640d's N57 engine, have the timing chain inspected immediately - preventative replacement at £1,250-£2,100 is far more cost-effective than a full engine replacement. For higher-mileage 640d examples approaching 100,000 miles, we recommend budgeting for preventative timing chain work as a maintenance item rather than waiting for failure.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N57D30 BMW 6 Series 640d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Failure - Coolant Leaks and Fire Risk in the BMW 6 Series 640d
problems.rootCause: Carbon buildup and thermal cycling cause the EGR cooler to crack, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust system. This can lead to coolant loss, overheating, and in worst cases, engine bay fires.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of EGR cooler and associated gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective fix; check if vehicle is covered by BMW recall

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If EGR failure has caused overheating or coolant contamination

problems.vehicleValueCheck: BMW issued a recall for EGR cooler replacement on many N57-equipped vehicles. Check if your BMW 6 Series 640d has had the recall work completed before paying for repairs out of pocket. For vehicles where the EGR cooler has failed and caused engine damage, evaluate replacement cost against the vehicle's £9,000-£22,000 value band.
problems.recommendation: If your BMW 6 Series 640d is losing coolant without visible external leaks, or if you notice rough running and the engine warning light, have the EGR system inspected immediately. BMW's recall programme covers many vehicles - check your VIN with a main dealer before authorising any paid repair.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Boost Issues - Loss of Power in the BMW 6 Series 640d
problems.rootCause: The N57's twin-turbo system relies on vacuum-operated pressure converters and boost solenoids. Perished vacuum lines and failed pressure converters are common causes of intermittent boost loss and drivetrain errors.

repairOptions.tier: Vacuum line and pressure converter replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of perished vacuum lines and failed boost solenoids
repairOptions.longevity: First-line fix; addresses most intermittent boost issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuild or replacement of failed turbo unit
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo itself has failed due to oil starvation or wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt N57 with upgraded turbo components
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has caused metal contamination throughout engine

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With BMW 6 Series 640d values ranging from £9,000-£22,000, turbo repairs are generally worthwhile for most owners. However, if the turbo has failed and sent metal debris through the engine, a full replacement may be the only safe option.
problems.recommendation: Intermittent boost loss on the BMW 6 Series 640d is often caused by simple vacuum line perishing or failed pressure converters. Start with a specialist diagnostic check before assuming the turbo itself has failed - many 640d owners have resolved boost issues for under £500.
